name: Twin Home Buyer - Inbound Seller Call Standard

categories.name: Opening & Rapport
categories.what_good_looks_like: Rep identifies themselves and the company, thanks the seller for calling, and spends the first 60-90 seconds listening rather than pitching.
criteria: Introduced self and Twin Home Buyer by name
Asked an open question before offering anything
Let the seller finish without interrupting

categories.name: Motivation Discovery
categories.what_good_looks_like: Rep uncovers WHY the seller is selling and what happens if they do nothing. At least three motivation questions, including one follow-up that goes a layer deeper.
criteria: Asked why the seller is considering selling
Asked at least one follow-up that goes deeper than the first answer
Uncovered the real pain (burden, distance, cost, family pressure)
Asked what happens if they don't sell

categories.name: Property & Condition
categories.what_good_looks_like: Rep gets enough condition detail to underwrite: beds/baths, square footage, roof, systems, kitchen/bath, and anything deferred.
criteria: Asked beds / baths / square footage
Asked about condition and needed repairs
Asked about roof, HVAC, plumbing, or electrical specifically
Asked about occupancy (vacant, owner-occupied, tenant)

categories.name: Timeline
categories.what_good_looks_like: Rep pins down a real date or event, not 'sometime'. Tests the timeline with a follow-up.
criteria: Asked when the seller wants this handled
Pushed past a vague answer to a date, month, or triggering event
Connected the timeline to the seller's motivation

categories.name: Decision Makers
categories.what_good_looks_like: Rep confirms everyone on title and everyone whose opinion matters, and gets them onto the next call.
criteria: Asked who else is on title or involved in the decision
Named the other decision maker back to the seller
Proposed getting that person on the next call

categories.name: Price & Offer Anchoring
categories.what_good_looks_like: Rep gets the seller to name a number first, anchors against condition and certainty, and never blurts a number before understanding motivation.
criteria: Got the seller to say a number first
Asked how the seller arrived at that number
Framed the offer around speed, certainty, and as-is condition, not just price
Did NOT give a number in the first three minutes
signals: how did you come up with

categories.name: Objection Handling
categories.what_good_looks_like: Rep acknowledges the objection, asks a question back, then reframes. No arguing, no discounting the seller's number head-on.
criteria: Acknowledged the objection before responding
Asked a clarifying question instead of arguing
Reframed around certainty, condition, or net proceeds

categories.name: Clear Next Step
categories.what_good_looks_like: The call ends with a specific commitment: a day, a time, and who will be on it. 'I'll call you back sometime' does not count.
criteria: Proposed a specific next step
Named a day and time
Confirmed the seller agreed
Confirmed best callback number or email

categories.name: Call Control & Talk Ratio
categories.what_good_looks_like: Seller talks more than the rep. Rep asks more questions than they make statements, and steers the call back on track after tangents.
criteria: Seller talk time is greater than rep talk time
Rep asked at least 8 questions
Rep steered back after a tangent

auto_fail: Rep gave a specific dollar offer before asking why the seller is selling
Rep ended the call with no next step of any kind
Rep argued with or talked over the seller
